questions.question: How do you sum total fills grouped by symbol? (Think: GROUP BY + SUM)
questions.setup_code: # Table trades(trade_id INT, symbol VARCHAR, fill_quantity INT)
options: SELECT symbol, SUM(fill_quantity) AS total_fills FROM trades GROUP BY symbol;
SELECT symbol, SUM(fill_quantity) AS total_fills FROM trades;
SELECT SUM(fill_quantity) AS total_fills FROM trades GROUP BY symbol;
SELECT symbol, COUNT(fill_quantity) AS total_fills FROM trades GROUP BY symbol;
questions.explanation: You need SUM(fill_quantity) and then GROUP BY symbol to get the total fills per symbol.

questions.question: How would you query executions for a strategy over the last week? (Hint: time-based filter with INTERVAL)
questions.setup_code: # Table executions(exec_id INT, strategy VARCHAR, exec_time TIMESTAMP)
options: SELECT * FROM executions WHERE strategy = 'XYZ' AND exec_time >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 DAY';
SELECT * FROM executions WHERE strategy = 'XYZ' AND exec_time > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 DAYS';
SELECT * FROM executions WHERE exec_time >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND strategy = 'XYZ';
SELECT * FROM executions WHERE strategy = 'XYZ' AND exec_time BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 DAY' AND CURRENT_DATE;
questions.explanation: Use CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 DAY' to filter rows from the last 7 days, combined with the strategy condition.

questions.question: Explain INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN using trades and fills. (Think: matching vs unmatched data)
questions.setup_code: # Tables: trades(trade_id INT, ...) and fills(fill_id INT, trade_id INT, ...)
options: INNER JOIN returns only matching rows; LEFT JOIN returns all from the left table even if no match.
INNER JOIN returns all left rows regardless of matches; LEFT JOIN returns only matching rows.
INNER JOIN includes unmatched rows from both tables; LEFT JOIN excludes unmatched rows from the left table.
INNER JOIN returns unmatched rows only; LEFT JOIN returns all rows but without duplicates.
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN keeps only matching rows, while LEFT JOIN keeps all rows from the left table and fills with NULL when there’s no match.

questions.question: Write a query to calculate daily P&L per trader. (Hint: use CASE WHEN for side logic)
questions.setup_code: # Table trades(trade_date DATE, trader_id INT, side VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, qty INT)
options: SELECT trade_date, trader_id, SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'SELL' THEN price * qty WHEN side = 'BUY' THEN -price * qty ELSE 0 END) AS pnl FROM trades GROUP BY trade_date, trader_id;
SELECT trade_date, trader_id, SUM(price * qty) AS pnl FROM trades GROUP BY trade_date, trader_id;
SELECT trade_date, trader_id, SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'BUY' THEN price * qty WHEN side = 'SELL' THEN price * qty END) AS pnl FROM trades GROUP BY trade_date, trader_id;
SELECT trade_date, trader_id, SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'SELL' THEN -price * qty WHEN side = 'BUY' THEN price * qty ELSE 0 END) AS pnl FROM trades GROUP BY trade_date, trader_id;
questions.explanation: You need a CASE WHEN that makes SELL positive and BUY negative, then SUM and GROUP BY trade_date and trader_id.

questions.question: How do you detect duplicate trade IDs? (Clue: GROUP BY and HAVING COUNT > 1)
options: SELECT trade_id FROM trades GROUP BY trade_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
SELECT trade_id FROM trades WHERE COUNT(trade_id) > 1;
SELECT trade_id FROM trades HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
SELECT trade_id, COUNT(*) FROM trades GROUP BY trade_id WHERE COUNT(*) > 1;
questions.explanation: Use GROUP BY trade_id and then HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 to filter only those trade_ids that appear more than once.

questions.question: Write a query to find clients with zero trades. (Hint: LEFT JOIN with IS NULL)
questions.setup_code: # Tables: clients(client_id INT), trades(trade_id INT, client_id INT)
options: SELECT c.client_id FROM clients c LEFT JOIN trades t ON c.client_id = t.client_id WHERE t.trade_id IS NULL;
SELECT client_id FROM clients WHERE client_id NOT IN (SELECT client_id FROM trades);
SELECT c.client_id FROM trades t RIGHT JOIN clients c ON t.client_id = c.client_id WHERE t.trade_id IS NULL;
SELECT c.client_id FROM clients c JOIN trades t ON c.client_id = t.client_id WHERE t.trade_id = NULL;
questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN keeps all clients and NULLs for no match; filtering WHERE t.trade_id IS NULL returns only those with no trades.

questions.question: Explain the difference between WHERE and HAVING. (Think: before vs after aggregation)
options: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
WHERE filters groups after grouping; HAVING filters rows before grouping.
WHERE and HAVING are interchangeable when filtering aggregated data.
WHERE can be used only with GROUP BY; HAVING only without GROUP BY.
questions.explanation: WHERE applies to individual rows before GROUP BY; HAVING applies to the grouped results after aggregation.

questions.question: What's the difference between UNION and UNION ALL in trade reporting? (Clue: duplicates vs performance)
options: UNION removes duplicates and is slower; UNION ALL keeps all rows and is faster.
UNION ALL removes duplicates and is slower; UNION keeps all rows and is faster.
UNION orders results; UNION ALL does not maintain order.
Both remove duplicates but UNION ALL uses more memory.
questions.explanation: UNION deduplicates which adds overhead; UNION ALL simply concatenates both results without checking for duplicates.

questions.question: What kind of index would you use for a high-volume trade table queried by symbol and time? (Clue: composite index)
options: CREATE INDEX idx_symbol_time ON trades(symbol, trade_time);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_symbol_time ON trades(symbol, trade_time);
questions.explanation: A composite index on (symbol, trade_time) speeds up queries filtering by both columns together.

questions.question: Write a query to compute net position using CASE WHEN. (Hint: BUY adds, SELL subtracts)
questions.setup_code: # Table trades(symbol VARCHAR, side VARCHAR, quantity INT)
options: SELECT symbol, SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'BUY' THEN quantity WHEN side = 'SELL' THEN -quantity ELSE 0 END) AS net_position FROM trades GROUP BY symbol;
SELECT symbol, SUM(quantity) AS net_position FROM trades GROUP BY symbol;
SELECT symbol, SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'SELL' THEN quantity WHEN side = 'BUY' THEN -quantity END) AS net_position FROM trades GROUP BY symbol;
SELECT symbol, SUM(CASE side WHEN 'BUY' THEN quantity WHEN 'SELL' THEN -quantity END) AS net_position FROM trades GROUP BY symbol;
questions.explanation: Use CASE WHEN to add BUY quantities and subtract SELL quantities, then GROUP BY symbol to aggregate.
